Ramirez Baker and Christensen Clinic
Re: Jason Sampson (DOB 11/06/1968)

January 23, 2026

Dear Jason Sampson (DOB 11/06/1968)

Mr. Jason Sampson, born on November 6, 1968, presented to my office on January 23, 2026, with a follow-up visit concerning his benign tumor and polyps. During this visit, his blood pressure was recorded at 131/78, and his weight was 224 pounds. Mr. Sampson is doing well and continues to manage his condition effectively.

His medical history includes a diagnosis of benign with high-grade dysplasia, which was first noted on April 15, 2025. His prostate cancer, initially diagnosed on January 27, 2023, is currently under surveillance. The Gleason score for his prostate cancer is 6, and the PSA levels have remained undetectable. The stage of the prostate cancer was not stated, and Mr. Sampson has been under surveillance for approximately 2.1 years since his treatment.

On September 5, 2025, Mr. Sampson returned for another check-up related to his benign tumor and polyps. His blood pressure was 131/82, and his weight was 225 pounds. He was doing well at that time as well.

Further back, on April 17, 2025, he came in with a complaint of back strain. His blood pressure at that visit was 131/83, and his weight was 211 pounds. He was doing well and has since recovered from the strain.

On November 28, 2024, Mr. Sampson visited for a follow-up concerning his cancer. His blood pressure was 119/73, and his weight was 211 pounds. He continued to do well. On July 10, 2024, he returned with a rash. His blood pressure was 123/84, and his weight was 218 pounds. The rash has since resolved.

On February 20, 2024, Mr. Sampson was again for his benign tumor and polyps. His blood pressure was 124/84, and his weight was 221 pounds. He was doing well.

Mr. Sampson's medical history also includes a diagnosis of benign tumor with high-grade dysplasia. On October 3, 2023, he visited for his cancer surveillance. His blood pressure was 121/73, and his weight was 225 pounds. He has been under surveillance for approximately 2.1 years since his treatment for prostate cancer, which has Gleason score 6, and his PSA levels have remained undetectable.

On May 15, 2023, Mr. Sampson visited for a medication refill. His blood pressure was 125/75, and his weight was 223 pounds. He was doing well at that time.

On December 26, 2022, he returned for his surveillance. His blood pressure was 131/74, and his weight was 222 pounds. Mr. Sampson has been under surveillance for 2.1 years since his treatment for prostate cancer, w
